errors.title: Timestamp ordering discards accepted fractional precision beyond microseconds
errors.observed: The public stage command accepts created_at 2026-09-07T00:00:00.5000002Z and reviewed_at 2026-09-07T00:00:00.5000001Z, returning exit 0 and writing a complete supported generation. The review instant is 100 nanoseconds earlier than creation. Later and equal-instant controls at the same precision also stage, so this is an ordering failure rather than a general unsupported-format rejection.
errors.cause: The shared UTC grammar accepts an arbitrary nonempty decimal fraction. datetime.fromisoformat retains only microseconds; converting before comparison erases the digits that distinguish these two valid inputs.
errors.expected: Compare the full accepted precision without truncation. Any alternative precision restriction must be explicit and consistent at the input boundary, with a reasoned contract decision rather than silently accepting values and comparing different instants. Retain exact earlier/later/equal controls and the repaired ordinary fractional cases.
